sample/ask: A model answers a question by sampling. Asked seven times eight, it says fifty six half the time, fifty four three times in ten, and sixty four the rest: its probabilities, written with the Greek letter pi.
sample/reward: A checker scores each answer: a reward, R, of one when it is right and zero when it is wrong. It is just a number, with nothing to differentiate.
sample/goal: Training should raise the expected reward, J: each answer's probability times its R, added up. Here zero point five times one, plus zeros: zero point five. Its gradient would say how to change the model's parameters, written theta.
sample/stuck: But theta reaches the reward only through which answer gets sampled, and a random draw has no slope.
trick/sum: Write J as a sum over every answer y: pi of y times R of y. Only the probabilities depend on theta, so the gradient of J is each reward times the gradient of its probability.
trick/one: Take one answer and one parameter. Here theta is three scores, one per answer, through a softmax. theta zero is the first, the score of fifty six, whose probability is zero point five.
trick/nudge: Nudge theta zero up by zero point zero one, and pi of fifty six rises to zero point five oh two five: a slope of zero point two five, written partial pi, partial theta zero.
trick/chain: Now the slope of its log. ln pi is ln u, with pi as the inside, u. The slope of ln u is one over u, so by the chain rule, partial ln pi, partial theta zero is partial pi, partial theta zero divided by pi: zero point two five over zero point five, which is zero point five.
trick/back: Run it backwards: the slope of pi is pi times the slope of its log. zero point five times zero point five gives back zero point two five.
trick/trick: That holds for every answer and every parameter: the gradient of pi is pi times the gradient of ln pi. This is the log trick.
try/p1: Try one. For one parameter, theta zero, an answer y has pi of y of zero point two, and partial pi, partial theta zero of zero point one six. What is partial ln pi, partial theta zero?
try/a1: Divide the slope of pi by pi: zero point one six over zero point two is zero point eight.
